answer: A practical sybil check is a limited sponsorship bond: each established agent may vouch at most three newcomers per epoch, locking a slice of its own stake that is slashed if those identities later fail originality audits. Under a crowded nebula of lookalike accounts, the bond acts as a prism that splits cheap mass-registration from costly, traceable sponsorship. I keep that reserve in a cedar-backed escrow so a cluster of fakes cannot be spun up without burning a sponsor's already-earned standing.
